### §104A. Copyright in restored works

(a) Automatic Protection and Term.—

(1) Term.—

(A) Copyright subsists, in accordance with this section, in restored works, and vests automatically on the date of restoration.

(B) Any work in which copyright is restored under this section shall subsist for the remainder of the term of copyright that the work would have otherwise been granted in the United States if the work never entered the public domain in the United States.

(2) Exception.—Any work in which the copyright was ever owned or administered by the Alien Property Custodian and in which the restored copyright would be owned by a government or instrumentality thereof, is not a restored work.

(b) Ownership of Restored Copyright.—A restored work vests initially in the author or initial rightholder of the work as determined by the law of the source country of the work.

(c) Filing of Notice of Intent to Enforce Restored Copyright Against Reliance Parties.—On or after the date of restoration, any person who owns a copyright in a restored work or an exclusive right therein may file with the Copyright Office a notice of intent to enforce that person's copyright or exclusive right or may serve such a notice directly on a reliance party. Acceptance of a notice by the Copyright Office is effective as to any reliance parties but shall not create a presumption of the validity of any of the facts stated therein. Service on a reliance party is effective as to that reliance party and any other reliance parties with actual knowledge of such service and of the contents of that notice.

(d) Remedies for Infringement of Restored Copyrights.—

(1) Enforcement of copyright in restored works in the absence of a reliance party.—As against any party who is not a reliance party, the remedies provided in chapter 5 of this title shall be available on or after the date of restoration of a restored copyright with respect to an act of infringement of the restored copyright that is commenced on or after the date of restoration.

(2) Enforcement of copyright in restored works as against reliance parties.—As against a reliance party, except to the extent provided in paragraphs (3) and (4), the remedies provided in chapter 5 of this title shall be available, with respect to an act of infringement of a restored copyright, on or after the date of restoration of the restored copyright if the requirements of either of the following subparagraphs are met:

ExhaustiveEnumPolicyMatrix  | `ExhaustiveEnumPolicyMatrix.lhs`  | Compiler-assisted policy review for generated enum roles and permissions

#### Actor Predicate Vocabulary

Raw source: Patterns/Haskell/ActorPredicateVocabulary.lhs

##### Pattern intent and mechanism

Define the bottom-most authentication layer as named predicates over `Maybe User`. This separates presence (authentication) from privilege (authorization) and provides render-gates for HSX.

The mechanism:

  1. Primitive predicates: `isLoggedIn`, `isMember`, `isAdmin :: Maybe User -> Bool` defined against their own primitive decision points. `isLoggedIn` is presence (`isJust`); privilege predicates use exhaustive enum classifiers, not each other.
  2. Exhaustive privilege classification: each privilege predicate classifies every current privilege constructor with a complete pattern match. A module-local `-Werror=incomplete-patterns` turns enum growth into a build failure at the classification site.
  3. Render gates: positive-only `whenLoggedIn`, `whenAdmin` for HSX with scope rule: `whenAdmin` is global admin chrome; per-resource gating stays on the permission/role axis.
  4. Axis separation: Presence/authentication ≠ privilege/authorization.

##### Project-specific notes and rollout guidance

Scope rule. `whenAdmin` controls global admin UI chrome (headers, navigation). Do not use it for per-resource authorization decisions; keep those on the `ScopedRolePermissionRegistry` axis.

Bit-rot safety. When extending the user role enum (e.g., adding `Moderator`), update each privilege predicate's exhaustive classifier. `isLoggedIn` stays `isJust` because presence is enum-independent. The compiler, not a runtime test, should fail if a privilege constructor has not been consciously classified.

HSX hygiene. Render gates return `Html`; their negative branch is `mempty`. If a view needs both branches, introduce an explicitly named local choice helper (`ifLoggedIn`, `authChoice`) rather than widening the `when...` gate.

##### Supporting snippets

Primitive presence predicate:
    
    `isLoggedIn :: Maybe User -> Bool
    isLoggedIn = isJust`

Exhaustive privilege classifiers:
    
    `{-# OPTIONS_GHC -Werror=incomplete-patterns #-}
    
    isMember :: Maybe User -> Bool
    isMember = maybe False (roleIsMember . userRole)
      where
        roleIsMember Member = True
        roleIsMember Admin  = False
    
    isAdmin :: Maybe User -> Bool
    isAdmin = maybe False (roleIsAdmin . userRole)
      where
        roleIsAdmin Admin  = True
        roleIsAdmin Member = False`

Adding `Moderator` to `Role` now breaks the build until every classifier handles it explicitly.

Render gates for HSX:
    
    `whenLoggedIn :: Maybe User -> Html -> Html
    whenLoggedIn mUser html =
        if isLoggedIn mUser then html else mempty
    
    whenAdmin :: Maybe User -> Html -> Html
    whenAdmin mUser html =
        if isAdmin mUser then html else mempty`


Admin bypass stays visible. If global admin bypass exists, keep it at the outer `can` function so the enum matrix remains about scoped role semantics.

Derived lists. Lists are allowed when they are derived from exhaustive classifiers or ranks over a total enum universe. In IHP, generated enums usually provide `Enum` and `Bounded`, so `filter roleIsAssignmentChoice [minBound .. maxBound]` and `sortOn roleDisplayRank [minBound .. maxBound]` are acceptable: a new constructor must first be classified by the helper. If the enum has no total enumeration, introduce a reviewed universe mechanism first; do not fall back to ad-hoc handwritten lists. Handwritten authority or UI lists are the anti-pattern.

Always-false policies still get names. If a domain axis matters, name an exhaustive predicate even when every current constructor returns `False`. A catch-all `_ -> False` reintroduces the blind spot. The name documents the policy question and creates the compiler tripwire for future roles.

Implicit policy names are a good outcome. Applying this pattern often turns anonymous list logic into domain vocabulary. Names such as `roleCanEditLinkedResource`, `roleGetsFullWorkspacePolicy`, or `roleIsAssignmentChoice` are more reviewable than `[Maintainer, Owner]` or `role == Owner`.

Do not over-apply. Mechanical enum lists are fine when new constructors should automatically appear with no domain review. Use this pattern when the enum carries policy, salience, eligibility, rank, or another meaning that must be consciously assigned.

Generated-enum rollout. When an IHP schema migration adds an enum value, regenerate types, then load the authorization or classification module in GHCi. Set local `OPTIONS_GHC -Werror=incomplete-patterns -Werror=unused-imports` in that module so the check works even when the interactive GHCi path does not inherit stricter project build flags. The failing helper names become the review checklist for the new role.

This pattern complements `ScopedRolePermissionRegistry`: that pattern defines where scoped role decisions live; this pattern defines how generated enum roles inside that registry should be classified.

For normal HTMX work, read the affected native reference page first. Before a version update, also inspect the release and migration notes and the exact versioned source. Use https://four.htmx.org/llms-full.txt as a mutable latest corpus for migrations, version changes, or broad agent audits; do not load the full corpus for every focused task, and do not treat it as versioned evidence.

Apply findings in a real host and verify the relevant browser/server invariants before changing canonical patterns. Machine-readable upstream material improves discovery but does not replace the local ordng canon, a pinned source revision, compilation, generated-asset checks, or browser verification.

Layer  | Role  | Files
--- | --- | ---
Shared  | Cross-pattern selector vocabulary  | `Shared/Types.lhs`
Primitives  | Single HTMX mechanism or response contract  | `Primitives/*.lhs`
Composed interactions  | Multi-part UI flows built from primitives  | `Composed/*.lhs`
Migration references  | Source/reference material for translation work  | `Migration/*.lhs`

Common composition chains:

  * `HtmxRequestMetadata` + `FilterTarget` → `TargetedPartialSectionFilter`
  * `FilterTarget` + `Indicator` → `Typeahead`
  * `Typeahead` + optional `Modal`/`OobUpdates` → `AssociationTable`

  * `InlineEditBoundary` + `Typeahead` + `OobUpdates` → `InlineRelationTypeaheadEdit`
  * `InlineDropdown` / `InlineButtonGroup` → `PermissionAwareEnumControl`
  * `OobUpdates` + `AccessibilityFocusAndLiveFeedback` for result-count or cross-region feedback
